On the right, “Today”: the same page with the same “Code”, and a blue arrow pointing to a blue puzzle piece labelled “Add-on”, the remedy that is still needed.
piezas.titular: Gemini’s formulas reached Google Docs as code; a year on, Docs still does not understand LaTeX
piezas.entradilla: In November 2025, Gemini was already writing and editing formulas in LaTeX, but when they were taken into Google Docs they arrived as code. A year on, Google’s word processor still cannot read LaTeX and the remedy is the same: an add-on or a separate editor.
cuerpo: On 11 November 2025, in ChatGPT-IA-edu, people were welcoming the [new LaTeX features in Gemini](https://workspaceupdates.googleblog.com/2025/10/new-latex-features-in-gemini-app.html), announced on 27 October: copying formulas, editing them in Canvas and generating PDFs. But when exporting to Google Docs the formulas were not converted, and when copied they came out as plain text. Secondary-school maths teachers were already asking about it. That same day, Juanjo de Haro presented EdiMarkWeb, a Markdown editor that converted LaTeX into DOCX, ODT or HTML.

A year on, the problem is where it was. The [Google Docs help page](https://support.google.com/docs/answer/160749?hl=en) explains equations through the Insert menu and with backslash shortcuts, without mentioning LaTeX. In January 2026, [Eric Curts](https://www.controlaltachieve.com/2026/01/export-math.html) found that Gemini’s export still left the code in view and recommended an add-on. And the listing for another, [MathInk](https://workspace.google.com/marketplace/app/mathink_for_docs_and_slides/539374951798), updated on 30 October 2026, puts it bluntly: Docs and Slides do not natively support LaTeX.

The editor, at least, has changed: it is now called [EdiMarkdown](https://edimarkdown.github.io/), with a desktop version and a formula editor of its own. That the workaround of back then is still the solution also says how far each thing has come.

piezas.comprobado: Verificador, contra la entrada: mensajes #41929-#41958 de ChatGPT-IA-edu del 11/11/2025 (novedades de LaTeX, queja por la exportación a Docs y el texto plano al copiar #41935 y #41937, pregunta de docentes de secundaria #41938, EdiMarkWeb #41940 y #41958). Telegram embed de #41929 y #41940: son esos mensajes, del 11/11/2025. Workspace Updates (WebFetch): 27/10/2025; PDF, edición en Canvas con fx, copia del código sin renderizar; no nombra Google Docs. Ayuda de Docs 160749 (WebFetch): ecuaciones desde Insertar > Símbolos > Ecuación y atajos con barra invertida; no menciona LaTeX. Control Alt Achieve (WebFetch): 28/01/2026, copiar y “Export to Docs” dejan código; recomienda Auto-LaTeX Equations. Ficha de MathInk (WebFetch): Docs y Slides no admiten LaTeX de forma nativa, actualizada el 30/10/2026; WebSearch sin anuncio oficial de soporte nativo. edimarkweb.github.io (WebFetch): “Ahora está en edimarkdown.github.io”; allí, EdiMarkdown de Juan José de Haro, escritorio v3.5.5 y editor de fórmulas EdiCuaTeX. Nada en publicado.txt sobre el tema; no repite NotebookLM, Veo, artefactos de Claude ni Kimi. 232 palabras con la entradilla.
repaso: Corregido: la ficha de MathInk se presentaba como “uno de ellos” (el complemento que recomienda Curts); Curts recomienda Auto-LaTeX Equations, así que ahora dice “la ficha de otro”.
